candidate.name: purejsimage
candidate.distributionReview: OPEN: the package archive includes optional HEIF/HEIC codec code; review complete notices, distribution scope, and the upstream patent note before considering approval.

method.fixtureGeneration: Candidate public JPEG encoder generated synthetic fixtures; APP2 segments padded each file to within 1-3 bytes of the 20 MiB input limit.
method.decoderOutput: Streamed rgb8 pixel blocks were assembled into an exact 64000000-byte RGBA buffer inside the worker and retained until after PeakWorkingSet64 sampling.

behavior.truncatedImageData: Both fixtures failed with ImageError: JPEG ended before image data.
behavior.abortSignal: After AbortSignal was aborted during async iteration, the decoder yielded another block; the decoder itself did not honor the signal.
behavior.iteratorReturn: Calling the async iterator return() completed.
behavior.cancellationGate: Any integration must prove timely cancellation by ending iteration or terminating and retiring the utilityProcess; this spike did not validate the production cancellation path.

decision.nextStep: Candidate merits a separate T06 dependency and distribution review before any installation or production integration.

limitations: One sample per fixture is feasibility evidence, not a stable peak-memory distribution or a hard 256 MiB process limit.
Synthetic fixtures were encoded by the candidate package; no independent pixel oracle was used, so the recorded output hashes identify outputs but do not independently establish decoder fidelity.
The 64 MB RGBA output was not transferred to the parent process and the candidate was not loaded from a packaged ASAR.
Progressive JPEG, EXIF, ICC, orientation, broad content variation, and the complete product pipeline were not tested.
Measurement harnesses and source fixtures remain in the local TEMP audit directory and are not archived in the repository; raw JSON measurements were transcribed into this evidence record.
